newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hurricane Hernan swirls off Mexico's Pacific coast.
newsitem.headline: Hurricane Hernan swirls off Mexico's Pacific coast.

text.p: Hurricane Hernan, forcing a maximum state of alert for coastal communities and shipping, is poised to pounce on Mexico's Pacific Coast, authorities said Wednesday.

"Continuing its current trajectory, it is expected that the center of Hurricane Hernan will be just 15 km (9 miles) south-south east of Manzanillo in the state of Colima at 1600 local/2100 GMT," the National Meterological Service said in an update.
Manzanillo is one of the major Pacific ports and is currently one of several closed to shipping.
Packing sustained winds of 140 km per hour (87 mph) and gusts of 160 km per hour (100 mph), Hernan is currently edging northeasterly at 12 km per hour (7.5 mph).

TV weather forecasters are predicting the eye of the hurricane will touch land inside four hours, although already tails spinning off from the center are dumping heavy rains and whipping up heavy seas.
Alerts are out along the coast from Acapulco in Guerrero state to coastal areas around Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco state, the meterological service said.
Waves of up to four meters have been reported by national media and rains of up to 7 cm (2 inches) are expected to be dumped across the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco states.
All are primary agricultural regions producing everything from corn, coffee to sugar. The region is also a prime livestock country, especially along the coast.
"Mudslides are expected in mountainous areas with flooding in the states of Guerrero and Michoacan," the service added.

One road has already been swept away along the Guerrero coast just outside Acapulco. A Guerrero state government spokesman said the road that connects the world famous tourist resort with Zihuatanejo in Guerrero state should be rebuilt inside three weeks.
Spokesmen from the state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos and from the Communications and Transportation Ministry were not immediately available to confirm which ports were closed.
The area affected by the hurricane is a long way from Mexico's crude oil ports on the Gulf of Mexico and minor terminals on the Pacific ocean side, which are much further to the south.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
